what_this_release_is: ATLAS is connected to the REAL Kalshi production account in READ_ONLY. Authentication, balance and reconciliation are verified against the live account. Zero broker writes. The full live SHADOW IS RUNNING on the deployment now in production: on 2026-09-19T09:38:20Z the engine produced a production WOULD_SUBMIT (KXBTC15M-26SEP190545-45 YES x1 @ 6c) on cycle 810, and a second at 09:54:37Z (KXBTC15M-26SEP190600-00 NO x1 @ 8c) on cycle 825. Both recorded risk_passed=1 and orders_submitted=0 with rejection reason prod_read_only -- the decision completed and the READ_ONLY cycle authorization stopped it before any call to the write path. 21 consecutive cycles around those events submitted nothing and filled nothing, and reconciliation read MATCH (broker=0 local=0) twice after them. These are the third and fourth confirmed shadow decisions; the first two were 2026-09-08T14:54:44Z and 2026-09-11T09:55:03Z on earlier deployments. The shadow remains deposit-dependent, not code-dependent: it was already running on two deployments that predate any shadow-scan merge, so the 2026-09-18 deployment of 033fb43 is not what started it. The F2 accounting design (a deposit must never clear a loss-derived guard) is still awaiting cross-audit. CAPITAL remains NOT authorized.

open_findings.summary: Provenance telemetry is computed but never logged. Binance klines returned HTTP 451 in 468 of 468 DEMO cycles and a fallback supplied data every cycle, but accepted providers log at DEBUG only, and data_quality_score, klines source, spot_sources and source_dispersion are never emitted. Which provider actually fed the model is unobservable from logs.
open_findings.consequence: The per-decision provenance fields the audit requires will be MISSING on the LIVE shadow stream until telemetry is added.

open_findings.summary: Railway's stored service builder reads RAILPACK while railway.json pins DOCKERFILE. The Dockerfile is what actually builds, but the two settings disagree and a future change to railway.json handling would silently switch builders.
The Dockerfile runtime stage ships run_tests.py, tests/ and _bootstrap.py into the deployed image. No execution path reaches them.
